facts.statement: Laricola was a genus of extinct birds resembling gulls that lived in Europe during the late Oligocene and early Miocene.
facts.quote: Laricola is a genus of extinct gull-like birds that lived during the late Oligocene and early Miocene in what is now Europe.

facts.statement: The genus Laricola was described by Mlíkovský in 2002.
facts.quote: Mlíkovský described the genus Laricola in 2002.

facts.statement: Milne-Edwards previously classified three species of Laricola as belonging to the genus Larus between 1863 and 1868.
facts.quote: Milne-Edwards (1863–1868) had previously classified three of the genus' members (Laricola elegans, L. totanoides, and L. desnoyersii) as Larus.

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Laricola is Laricola elegans, described by Milne-Edwards in 1868.
facts.quote: The type species is Laricola elegans (Milne-Edwards, 1868).

facts.statement: Laricola possessed proportionally longer and more slender legs than living species of the family Laromorphae.
facts.quote: Laricola have "proportionally longer and more slender legs" than extant species of the family Laromorphae.

facts.statement: Fossils of Laricola have been found in France and are also alleged to come from the Czech Republic.
facts.quote: Laricola fossils stem from France, and allegedly the Czech Republic.

facts.statement: The genus Laricola contains five distinct species.
Laricola intermedia is a species within the genus, described by De Pietri et al. in 2014.
Laricola robusta is a species within the genus, described by De Pietri et al. in 2014.
Laricola belongs to the parent group Laromorphae.
Laricola lived between the Rupelian and Aquitanian stages, from 33.9 to 20.45 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Rupelian to Aquitanian (33.9 to 20.45 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Laricola is classified within the class Aves.
